newsitem.title: USA: US says Iraq oil deal can't go forward as planned.
newsitem.headline: US says Iraq oil deal can't go forward as planned.

text.p: The United States said Tuesday that the planned limited oil sales by Iraq cannot go forward because there are no guarantees food and medicine financed from the sales would go to the people who need it.
Special Assistant to the President Mark Parris told reporters that until the United States is convinced that aid from the sales will go to the people who need it, "it can't go forward."

The oil-for-food plan allows Iraq to sell oil worth $2 billion over six months to purchase badly-needed food and medicine for its people, suffering under sanctions imposed when Iraq invaded Kuwait in August 1990.

Parris said the program was based on assurances that a certain amount of the aid would go to Kurdish areas now under Baghdad's control. He said the plan has to be revisited in light of weekend fighting in northern Iraq in which the Iraqi army and a Kurdish faction captured Arbil from a rival Kurdish group.
U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali on Sunday postponed implementation of the oil-for-food plan, expected later this month.
